5.1.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "why does a total hip dislocate?"
- "About **3%** of primary hips dislocate → most in the **first 3 months**, more after revision."
- "**Multifactorial** → design, **position**, soft-tissue tension, muscle disease · plus misuse or trauma."
- "Work-up → mechanism, timing, **exclude infection** → AP + lateral films → **CT** for version."

### Prevalence & timing
- Incidence → primary THA (total hip arthroplasty) ≈**1–3%** · revision **5–7%** (Miller, Prof Azzam)
[[FIG: Fig 5.1 · 5.1
- Timing → **75%** in the first year · ≈70% of these in the first **3 months** (Prof Azzam)
- Early → capsule and muscles still healing, muscle control not yet back
- Risk persists → ≈**1% per year** for 2–3 years · then ≈1% every 5 years

#### Early vs late
- **Late** (>5 years) → over half recurrent, most → revision
- Early first dislocation + well-placed parts → **closed reduction** usually enough · late ones recur more

#### THA vs hemiarthroplasty
- Neck fracture → THA has a **higher dislocation rate** than hemiarthroplasty (Miller)
- Hemiarthroplasty → safer when precautions fail → **dementia**, Parkinson disease
- THA still → best function in **active** elderly or pre-existing arthritis
- THA for neck fracture → **anterior or anterolateral** approach to cut dislocation (Campbell)

CLINICAL PEARL — mechanical, once infection is out
- Mostly **aseptic** → which determinant failed: design, position, tension or muscle?
- **Septic loosening** can present as recurrent dislocation → markers ± aspiration first
- Parvizi → still no answer after decades → **multifactorial**

### Factors contributing to instability
- Four determinants, their failures and dislocation direction → 4 Biomechanics
- **GT** (greater trochanter) **osteotomy** nonunion or proximal escape → abductors slack → recurrent instability
[[FIG: Fig 5.2 · 5.1

#### What the surgeon controls
- Also → primary stability, approach, tensioning + **capsular repair**, larger head, expertise
- **Anterior** approach dislocates less than **posterior** → many risk factors → lower-risk approach

#### Disease & time
- **DDH** (developmental dysplasia of the hip) → higher rate, several factors at once
[[FIG: Fig 5.3 · 5.1
- Years later → **polyethylene (PE) wear** + soft-tissue laxity more than malposition
- Wear → lower effective rim, shorter jump distance → a long-stable hip dislocates

#### Grading the cause — Dorr & Wera
| Type | Dorr (Prof Azzam) | Wera, 75 revisions (Campbell) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **positional** | acetabular malposition |
| 2 | **soft-tissue imbalance** | femoral malposition |
| 3 | **component malposition** | **abductor insufficiency** → most recurrence after revision |
| 4 | — | **impingement** |
| 5 | — | late wear |
| 6 | — | unresolved |

### External causes & precautions
- **Trauma** = outside force · **improper use** = extreme or forbidden positions
- Commonest dislocating positions → **crossing legs**, lying in **external rotation (ER)** (Prof Molham Mahmoud)
[[FIG: Fig 5.4 · 5.1

| Approach | Avoid | Leave the bed (Handbook) |
|---|---|---|
| **Posterior / posterolateral** | flexion >70–90° · IR · adduction · crossing legs | same side as surgery |
| **Anterior / anterolateral / lateral** | ER · hyperextension · adduction | opposite side |

- Posterior → flexion + adduction + IR together = **dislocating position** (Prof Molham Mahmoud)
[[FIG: Fig 5.5 · 5.1
- Triggers → low seat, bending to pick up → move the whole body or use a **reacher**
[[FIG: Fig 5.6 · 5.1
- Aids → **raised toilet seat**, chairs with arms → flexion stays in the safe range
- After primary THA with **posterior capsular repair** → precautions relaxed, no rise in dislocation

CLINICAL PEARL — education prevents the second dislocation
- Patient repeats the instructions at discharge and follow-up · assistive tools for bed transfers
- **Caregivers** are the safeguard in dementia, alcoholism, cognitive impairment

### History & examination
- **Mechanism** → trauma vs improper position (squatting, low toilet) · recent vs neglected · first vs recurrent
- Also → time since surgery, **approach**, incident position, signs of **infection**
- Infection suspected → markers → **aspirate** if positive or on clinical judgement
- Confirm → **severe pain**, rotated limb, LLD (limb-length discrepancy)

| Dislocation | Limb lies (Miller) |
|---|---|
| **Posterior** | short · flexed · adducted · internally rotated |
| **Anterior** | short · extended · externally rotated |

- **Neurovascular** exam → **sciatic** nerve (peroneal division) at risk posteriorly → test dorsiflexion before and after reduction
- **Cognition** → a non-compliant patient is not protected by a brace → implant must be stable by design
- Case → 55 years, **AVN** (avascular necrosis) → THA · posterior dislocation day 2, three times (Prof Azzam)

### Radiological assessment
- **AP pelvis** (both hips + proximal ⅓ femur) + **lateral** → AP alone cannot tell anterior from posterior (Handbook)
- Add **cross-table lateral** · **standing and sitting** films → spinopelvic mechanism
- Look for → small head–neck ratio, steep cup, retroversion · cup offset, **GT** union, fractures
- **Cup** → inclination, version, mediolateral and vertical position, head eccentric in the cup

#### Reading offset & version
- **Stem** → medial and vertical offset vs the other side
- Compare only on **rotationally identical** views → obturator foramen and pelvic shape (Prof Azzam)
[[FIG: Fig 5.7 · 5.1
- **CT** → malposition missed on films · most reliable for cup and stem version
[[FIG: Fig 5.8 · 5.1

#### When films look normal
- Normal films + recurrent dislocation → soft tissue → **MRI with MARS** (metal artefact reduction sequence)
- MARS → late instability, osteolysis, wear · abductor tendons and gluteal muscle

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **3% · 3 months · design–position–tension–muscle · anteverted front, retroverted back · infection out, CT for version**

5.2.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you treat a dislocated total hip?"
- "**Reduce within 24 h** → closed under sedation, open only if closed fails → fix fractures within days."
- "Exclude infection, find the **cause** → malposition or loosening = **revision** · otherwise adjuncts."
- "Adjuncts → larger head, liner change, **dual mobility** or constrained liner, **trochanteric advancement**."

### Treatment algorithm
- **<24 h** → reduction · **days** → fix fractures · **delayed** → conservative or revision (Handbook)
- Delay → sciatic stretch, rim damage, contracture → neglected >a few days often irreducible closed
- Forceful reduction → periprosthetic fracture, component dissociation → sedation or GA (general anaesthesia) with relaxation
- Decide calmly once the cause is found → **infection out first**

#### Delayed treatment by cause
| Cause | Treatment (Prof Azzam) |
|---|---|
| Positional / soft-tissue imbalance (Dorr 1–2) | no component revision → liner exchange, **elevated rim**, larger head, dual mobility, trochanteric advancement |
| Multifactorial / idiopathic | combine methods → **dual mobility** or **constrained** liner |
| **Abductor deficiency** | soft-tissue reconstruction |
| **Malposition / loosening** | **revision** |

- Clear mechanical cause → correct it · unclear → more than one method
[[FIG: Fig 5.9 · 5.2

CLINICAL PEARL — how each adjunct fails
- Constrained liner failure → 4 Biomechanics · intraprosthetic dislocation → 1 Implants
- **Elevated rim** raises jump distance one way → becomes a fulcrum the other way

### Reduction & bracing
- **Closed** → best in early, first-time dislocations · sedation usually enough, GA rarely
- Longitudinal traction under **image intensifier** → abduction → usually reduces (Prof Azzam)
[[FIG: Fig 5.10 · 5.2
- **Allis** → supine, hip and knee flexed, in-line thigh traction, assistant fixes the pelvis
- Then → stability and nerves → X-ray → brace · **open** reduction only if closed fails

#### Liner & brace
- PE liner may **dissociate** during dislocation → head eccentric in the shell → open reduction
[[FIG: Fig 5.11 · 5.2
- Hard-on-soft, joint opened → **change the liner** → notched rim wears fast (Handbook)
- Recurrent → **abduction brace** 20° abduction, flexion ≤60°, 6 weeks–3 months (Campbell)
[[FIG: Fig 5.12 · 5.2
- Brace → no proven benefit, poor compliance → a **pillow** suffices (Prof Molham Mahmoud)
[[FIG: Fig 5.13 · 5.2

PITFALL — brace in 20° of what?
- Handbook → "brace in ≈20° flexion"; course and Campbell → 20° abduction · avoid squatting, flexion >90°
- Say → "**abduction brace, 20° abduction, flexion limited to 60°, 6 weeks to 3 months**"

### Indications for revision
- **Recurrent instability** → >2 dislocations (Handbook)
- **Correctable defect** on films (poor offset, retroversion, design flaw) → revise after the 1st or 2nd
- No cause found → wait → blind revision → high **re-dislocation** rate
- Define first → position, offset, abductors, **impingement** (osteophyte, cement, heterotopic bone)
[[FIG: Fig 5.14 · 5.2

#### Malposition & loosening in practice
- **Malposition >10°** → revise that component (Prof Azzam)
- Head/liner exchange with a larger head → well-placed parts only · lecturer → use selectively
- Case → stable, then recurrent at **3 years** → loose stem · markers, aspiration negative → **long stem**
[[FIG: Fig 5.15 · 5.2

### Revision strategies
| Cause | Strategy (Handbook) |
|---|---|
| Small head | larger head, tripolar or **dual mobility** liner |
| Lateralised stem | centralise / medialise the tip |
| Wrong inclination | revise to **30–50°** |
| Wrong version | **10–15°** anteversion → within Lewinnek 15 ± 10° |
| Weak abductors | inferolateralise the GT · ↑ offset (longer neck, smaller neck–shaft angle) |
| Neuromuscular disease | **dual mobility** first · **constrained cup** as salvage → stability at the cost of motion |

- Large head today → ceramic or metal on highly cross-linked PE, not metal-on-metal (Miller)
- **Constrained** = last resort → treats the symptom, costs motion, stresses fixation (Miller)
[[FIG: Fig 5.16 · 5.2
- Shell kept → **larger head** · multifactorial or idiopathic → dual mobility or constrained
- **Dual mobility** often preferred → stable without locking the head

#### Soft tissue & failed constraint
- Proven **abductor deficiency** → **Achilles allograft** or synthetic graft
- **Trochanteric advancement** → GT osteotomised, fixed distally and laterally → re-tensions abductors
[[FIG: Fig 5.17 · 5.2
- Failed **constrained liner** → revise components → planned **dual mobility** construct (Prof Azzam)
[[FIG: Fig 5.18 · 5.2

### Resection arthroplasty (Girdlestone)
- Indications → poor cognition, non-ambulatory, active infection, failed revisions (Handbook)
- Last resort → multiple dislocations, severely debilitated, failed management (Prof Azzam)
- Whole prosthesis out → empty head–neck space · history → 1 Implants
[[FIG: Fig 5.19 · 5.2
- Cost → limb **several cm short**, walking aids · can be temporary → reimplantation worse than planned staging

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Reduce <24 h · new liner · >10° = revise · big head, dual mobility, advance · constrained last · Girdlestone**
